accordance.notes: accordancebible.com returned 403; features drawn from Accordance’s history page and reviews (some older). Exact current names of search features not verified.

ascension.notes: Harvous’ translation list (KJV, NKJV, ESV, NIV, NLT, NET…) may not include a Catholic edition with deuterocanonical books — worth a check before claiming fit for Catholic readers.

aura-bible.notes: The Reformed/Westminster grounding comes from Aura’s own site and a third-party review.

bible-gateway.notes: Translation/audio counts from biblegateway.com/app; Plus pricing intentionally omitted.

bible-notes.notes: biblenotesapp.com now redirects to biblenotesapp.org, which lists the iOS/Android apps as “coming soon” — confirm the app is actually shipping before publishing. The old copy’s live polls, feedback and prayer requests were not found on the current site, so they were dropped.

bible-ai.notes: Third-party sites say Theology Mode voices are styled after C. S. Lewis, Spurgeon and others; the App Store listing only says “theologians,” so names are left out.

bibledojo.notes: The BibleDojo site didn’t render for fetching; facts come from third-party write-ups. Reports in 2026 say only the Law genre is live, with nine more genres planned — hence “starting in biblical law.” Worth a quick check of the site.

blessed.notes: The old copy mentions custom prayer lists and social sharing; the site doesn’t confirm them, so they’re left out.

craft.notes: Craft Android support only appears in structured data on its site; left out.

dwell.notes: Dwell is often praised for background music and listen-along text, but the homepage didn’t confirm them, so they’re left out.

e-sword.notes: e-Sword also has Mac (e-Sword X), iPad (HD) and iPhone (LT) apps; ‘Where notes live’ row describes the PC edition — check phrasing.

esv-bible.notes: ESV app page link in the input 404s; please check the competitor link. Plan count varies by source (50+ / 60+), so it’s kept as ‘50+’. Narrator names (e.g. Kristyn Getty) not used.

faithstudy.notes: The site copy mentions videos; the App Store listing doesn’t, so videos are left out. FaithStudy is iPhone-only and from Forerunner Technology (HK), the publisher of Blessedid — the blessedid.com link carries no product info, so it’s worth a check that this is the intended app.

glorify.notes: Glorify’s premium tier name/price varies across sources (Glorify+ ~$59.99/yr reported); omitted. Journaling described by reviewers, not on the current homepage.

google-docs.notes: Google Docs feature claims (comments, suggestion mode, version history) are well known; not re-verified on a page this run.

hallow.notes: Hallow added Hallow AI (Feb 2026) and Kids Profiles (May 2026) per secondary sources; not used. Verify Pray25 naming is still current.

illuminate.notes: The site no longer describes “1,000+ teachings” or a specific tradition, so that claim from the old copy is dropped.

life-bible.notes: Pricing model not stated on lifebible.com; omitted. Life Bible is from Tecarta.

logos.notes: AI feature tiers (Premium and up) change often; not mentioned in copy.

lumen.notes: Feature details (ESV, community feed) come from a third-party review; Lumen’s own site is behind sign-in. Pricing is unpublished.

pray-com.notes: Pray.com’s prayer-request/community features are described by partner and secondary sources, not its current homepage — worth a quick check.

readscripture.notes: Could not confirm whether ReadScripture has any notes feature; table says ‘Not a focus’ — check. Free per App Store listing.

reflect.notes: Reflect is mid-transition: the original subscription app continues, while ‘Reflect Open’ (free, open-source Mac app, local Markdown, iCloud/Git sync, bring-your-own AI key) launched mid-2026 with iPhone in beta. Copy avoids encryption and calendar claims and prices; verify reflect.app wording before publishing.

spirit-notes.notes: spiritnotes.app redirects to spiritnotes.com; pricing isn’t stated on the site, so the model was left out.

youversion.notes: Version/language counts from youversion.com (3.5k+ versions, 2,300 languages). ‘Plans with friends’ is long-standing but not on the fetched page; a 2026 article calls it Community Plans.

sermonary.notes: Sermonary’s site now names its views Calendar, Study, Write, Present, Recap, Insights, Multiply; it no longer says ‘podium mode’ or ‘blocks’, so the copy uses the current names.

sermons-app.notes: Sermons.app also advertises ‘searchable sermon memory’ for illustrations and series threads, which overlaps Harvous; copy leans on the Bible reader instead.

band.notes: band.us could not be fetched directly; features taken from the App Store listing and release notes.

called.notes: Called pricing not stated on site (free trial/demo only); omitted.

wordgo.notes: Previous copy claimed a ‘per-course journal’; the official WordGo page doesn’t mention one (a third-party review mentions a private journal), so it was left out.

waha.notes: Waha’s official page didn’t state free/ad-free; that’s from AlternativeTo and faith.tools. Previous copy said 50+ languages; official page now says 63.

manna.notes: Manna (Blake Croft) also has a ‘Remember’ tab that resurfaces past notes and highlights — close to Harvous Suggestions, so resurfacing is not claimed as a difference. Native iPhone/iPad app vs Harvous web-only. Several unrelated apps share the name Manna; facts taken from the App Store listing that links gathermanna.com.

sermon-keeper.notes: Brief suggested 'Sermon Prep', but Sermon Keeper is a listener-side sermon notes app, so competitorType is set to 'Bible Notes'. Platform from site: iPhone only.

she-reads-truth.notes: App Store rating was low (~3.2) in snapshots; not mentioned. Third-party claims of a 'She Reads Truth+' tier were unverified and left out.

day-one.notes: App Store id 1044867788 is the iPhone/iPad/Mac listing; 1055511498 appears to be a separate Mac listing.

notability.notes: Notability Android availability reported in 2026; site lists iOS, Android, web, Mac, Windows.
